title: CIH 541 Sadd Maʾrib 5, lines 80–92 — Abraha's Maʾrib dam inscription, 548 CE: the ambassador of ROME arrives at the court of a South Arabian king, in the same sentence as the Negus, the king of Persia, and three Arab rulers
language_note:
Late Sabaic, `xsa` as `arabia-04-jabal-dabub` carries it. DASI's own classification on the record is "Ancient South Arabian » Sabaic » Late Sabaic", script "Ancient South Arabian", monumental, right-to-left, raised, incised.

WHAT IS REPRODUCED IS DASI'S TRANSLITERATION AND NOT THE MUSNAD. The record's TEXT panel prints the inscription in Latin-script transliteration with the corpus's editorial marks; the musnad itself is on the stone. `classify_original` returns `('transliteration', 'xsa', True)` and `english_marker_ratio` is **0.0** — measured, and zero because the passage is proper names and Sabaic particles from end to end.
date: 548 CE. THE DATE IS THE SOURCE'S AND IS NOT HEDGED HERE BECAUSE THE SOURCE DOES NOT HEDGE IT: DASI's chronology block gives Start date 548 CE, End date 548 CE, and "Date accuracy: Accurate", and its general note says "The inscription is dated to 548 CE." That is a dated South Arabian monument from inside Justinian's reign.

original_text_note:
Verbatim from the TEXT panel of the DASI/CSAI record for CIH 541 Sadd Maʾrib 5, https://dasi.cnr.it/project/1/epigraphs/2382, DOI 10.82194/dasi-epi-2382, read on 2026-09-06. Lines 80–92 of 136.

VERIFIED BY DIGEST, AS RECORD 44 WAS. The excerpt was typed into a file on the bridge and the same span sliced independently out of the live page in the browser; SHA-256 computed on both machines agrees at `d48ef25adba2a910996291d3…` on a length of 485 characters. The translation was checked the same way at 682 characters.

AND THE DIGEST CAUGHT SOMETHING A READER WOULD NOT HAVE. **The line-number gutter is made of NON-BREAKING SPACES, U+00A0, four per line, forty-four in this span**, and they are reproduced as the page renders them. A curator retyping this passage would have typed ordinary spaces and the record would have differed from its source in forty-four characters without a single visible difference. FINDINGS 48 and 50 are exactly this failure with a different codepoint. The gutter is kept as it is; nothing is normalised.

THE EDITORIAL MARKS ARE DASI'S AND ARE ALL KEPT: `—` at a line end is the corpus's broken-word mark and not punctuation; `( )` marks an uncertain or partial reading; `(( ))` marks a variant; `< >` at line 87 marks text supplied by the editor. Their definitions are quoted in `reference_translation`, from DASI's editorial criteria page, because that is where the loader chunks them.

THE CAPTURE IS NOT BLIND, AND HERE IT IS DOUBLY NOT. This session located and captured in one pass, as records 41–44 did. **In addition, F5 Part 3's browser pass 3 had already read this record's Sabaic text and the opening of its English translation into a session transcript**, which ruling 77 declared in advance: a capture made now is checked against a document rather than against a second independent reading. FINDING 55 is why that is stated rather than argued away.

THE READING IS UNCERTAIN AT TWO POINTS OF THIS PASSAGE AND THE SOURCE SAYS SO IN ITS OWN NOTATION, NOT IN THIS RECORD'S WORDS. DASI's editorial criteria, at https://dasi.cnr.it/editorial-criteria, define the two marks that appear above, verbatim:

"( )     Uncertain or partial reading: when one or more characters are discernable on the support, but are illegible or only partially decipherable."

"(())     Variant (alternative reading or interpretation): a portion of text that may have an alternative reading or interpretation, due to ambiguous characters or doubts regarding the interpretation of proper. All alternatives will be searchable in the text."

SO LINE 84's ḏ-(Ṯ)wlmn IS A NAME WHOSE FIRST LETTER THE EDITORS COULD NOT READ WITH CERTAINTY, AND TWO NAMED EDITORS READ IT AS A DIFFERENT LETTER. The apparatus criticus printed on the same record page says, verbatim:

"84	Glaser and CIH: (S²)wlmn."

Ṯ against S², in a South Arabian name, with both editions marking their own letter as uncertain. And line 81's ʿrmn((ʿrmn)) carries the source's own variant marker on the word for the dam. THE ENGLISH ABOVE HEDGES ITS OWN LINE 82 THE SAME WAY, in the translator's words and not in this record's: "the entourage (?) of his son (or: who had gathered around (?) his son)" — a question mark on the reading, an alternative introduced by "or:", and a second question mark inside the alternative.
reference_translation_note:
The CSAI translation, from the TRANSLATIONS panel of the same record, under the same CC BY 4.0 as the text. It is the corpus's own English and is published beside the text it translates.

THE RECORD CARRIES A SECOND TRANSLATION AND THIS RECORD DOES NOT USE IT. The panel offers `CSAI` and `Nebes 2005`; only the CSAI one is taken, because it is the one under the record's own licence. **Nebes 2005 was not opened.** No claim is made about how it reads these lines, and a record that quoted both without saying which it had read would be claiming a collation it never did.

THE GLOSS PARAGRAPH AT THE END OF `reference_translation` IS INSIDE THE CHUNKED FIELD ON PURPOSE. `notes` is not chunked and the model never sees it; F3 record 26 declared two gloss-capable records whose hedges were in `original_text_note` and neither could ever pass. The hedge, the named-editor alternative and the source's own statement that the reading is uncertain are therefore all in `reference_translation`, and every quoted sentence in it is DASI's.

"The above license applies to the data in this record, but not to any images displayed. The images are the property of third parties and are either used with permission or reproduced from publications (see the credits below each image)."

The licence named above that sentence is **CC BY 4.0**, printed on the epigraph record at https://dasi.cnr.it/project/1/epigraphs/2382, read on 2026-09-06.

THE POSITION IS `open_licence_stated` AND THE LICENCE IS VERSIONED, which record 44's is not: DASI prints `CC BY 4.0` and Hatke's front matter prints "the Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial License" with no version at all. Two `open_licence_stated` cells, two different degrees of precision, and the column records what each source printed rather than levelling them.

WHAT THE CARVE-OUT MEANS FOR THIS RECORD: nothing is taken but data. No image from the record is reproduced, linked as an asset, or described from the photograph. The exclusion is quoted because ruling 74 asks for the position stated verbatim and because a licence with an exception in it is not the same licence as one without.

AND THE REACHABILITY HISTORY IS PART OF THE RIGHTS STORY HERE. `F5_CANDIDATES.md` recorded DASI as "behind an Anubis anti-bot wall" that "returned 'Access Denied' to every route tried", and called it "the single most valuable thing lost in this hunt". A person with a browser was never challenged once. FINDING 69's distinction — REACHABLE is not LICENSED — has a mirror image, and this record is it: a source recorded as unreachable was open, and it was the automation and not the site that was refused.
findspot: Maʾrib, Yemen — the Great Dam. DASI gives Modern site `Maʾrib`, Ancient site `Mryb / Mrb`, Geographical area `Maʾrib`, Country `Yemen`, and archaeological context "Agricultural irrigation context: Dam or retaining structure". The stela is in the Mārib Museum, inv. nr. BAR 2.
notes:
F6, and the slot RULING 77 bought by exchanging a Persia `catalogue_record` slot with F7. **THIS RECORD CARRIES F6's ONE `gloss_capable` DECLARATION.**

IT BUYS NO FLOOR AND THAT WAS DECLARED BEFORE IT WAS TAKEN. Arabia stood at 5 against a floor of 4 and is now 6. The record is here for its provenance and its content, not for a count — ruling 77 says so in those words.

WHY THIS PASSAGE OF 136 LINES. Line 89: `mḥs²kt mlk Rmn`, the ambassador of the king of Rome, arriving at the court of a South Arabian king in 548 CE — **named in the same sentence as the Negus of Aksum, the king of Persia, and the envoys of al-Mundhir, of Ḥārith b. Jabala and of Abū Karib b. Jabala.** This corpus's premise is the world beyond the Roman Empire; here that world's own monumental record lists Rome as ONE DELEGATION AMONG SIX, in the order the stone puts it, after the Negus. The lines before it were kept for a reason: 80–81 bring the king back from the dam to the town of Mrb, which is what makes the court the delegations arrive at a place this record can place.

THE GLOSS, AND EVERY PIECE OF IT IS THE SOURCE'S. Line 84 prints `ḏ-(Ṯ)wlmn`, a name whose first letter DASI marks as an uncertain reading; the apparatus on the same page prints `84  Glaser and CIH: (S²)wlmn.`, two named editors reading a different letter; line 81 carries DASI's own variant marker on `ʿrmn((ʿrmn))`; and the English hedges its line 82 with a question mark and an alternative introduced by `or:`. The hedge AND the statement that the reading is uncertain both sit inside `reference_translation`, which the loader chunks — the mechanical requirement in full, on the standard `arabia-05-ruwafa` was declared on. `eastasia-05-liangshu-qin-lun` is the pattern for putting the paragraph where the model can see it.

SECOND DECLARATION REFUSED IN ADVANCE. `persia-06-shahrestaniha` and `scandinavia-07-rycksta-grikkium` both carry declarable material in chunked fields and NEITHER is declared, because `check_delivery` fails on the day a sub-tranche over-delivers. One declaration, one record, and F6's is this one.

THE PREDICTION THIS RECORD TESTS. Ruling 78's **P1**, written at `a20214e` before any F6 record existed: `tc-jabal-dabub` sat at rank 6 with zero slack, having fallen 3 → 6, with three chunks of `arabia-06-syllaeus` inside its window, and a FOURTH Arabia source-language record was predicted to push it out of the top 6 — which would move `ALL recall@6` off 0.727 for the first time since F4. P1 has been untestable all block because no Arabia record existed. **It is testable the moment this record is indexed.** Nothing here is gated on it.

AND A NOTE FOR WHOEVER READS THE RANKING RUN. This record puts TWO retrieval-eligible chunks into the index, both about a South Arabian monumental inscription naming Rome, which is what `tc-jabal-dabub` is about. If P1 confirms, FINDING 79's resemblance mechanism and FINDING 73's same-region mechanism BOTH predict it, and the run will not tell them apart. The Africa record placed the same day is the experiment that does — see ruling 78's P4.

findspot_places.name: Maʾrib (Mrb), the town the king returns to at line 81
findspot_places.note: `stated` because the excerpt's own line 81 names it — `hgrn Mrb`, the town of Mrb — and not only because DASI's site block does. THE ID WAS FOUND, CHECKED AND NOT ASSUMED. The 2026-08-10 Pleiades snapshot has no place TITLE matching 'Marib'; the id surfaced only through the names dump, as the attested Greek name `Μαρίαβα`, which is why `--names-dump` exists. Entry 39379 is titled `Mari(a)ba`, described "Capital of the Sabaean kingdom", located 15.427/45.336 at `precise`, feature types `ruin, settlement, tell`, attesting `roman` among its periods — which is Maʾrib, and agrees with DASI's Yemen/Maʾrib site record. A NAME MATCH IS NOT AN IDENTIFICATION and this one was confirmed on the description and the coordinate before it was taken; `--probe` could not be run because the proxy refuses pleiades.stoa.org, and that is a fact about this session's network and not about the id.

subject_places.name: Maʾrib — the court the six delegations arrive at
subject_places.note: The focus of the passage, and the reason lines 80–81 are inside the excerpt rather than left out: the king returns from the dam to the town of Mrb, and it is there that `wṣḥ-hmw`, they arrived. Without those two lines the arrivals would have no stated destination and every directional role below would be an assertion this record could not support — which is the refusal `scandinavia-07-rycksta-grikkium` earned on the other side, where a memorial does not say where a man set out from.

subject_places.name: Rmn — the king of Rome, whose ambassador arrives at line 89
subject_places.note: NO ID, AND SPECIFICALLY PLEIADES 423025 `Roma` IS NOT IMPORTED. `mlk Rmn` is the king of Rome, that is the Roman emperor and his state — Justinian, in 548 — and not the city on the Tiber. `persia-06-shahrestaniha` refused an id for `kēsar` because an office is not a city, `persia-05-abnun` refused one for `Hrōmāy` because a people is not a city, and `scandinavia-06-tjurko-bracteate` refused one for an adjective inside a compound. A STATE IS NOT A CITY EITHER. The connection is visible in the placement layer as an unplaced edge, which is what `regional` with a role and a note is for.

subject_places.name: Frs¹ — the king of Persia, whose mission arrives at line 90
subject_places.note: NO ID, for the reason above: `mlk Frs¹` is the Sasanian king and his realm, not a settlement. Recorded because the sentence's whole force is that ROME AND PERSIA SENT TO THE SAME COURT IN THE SAME SEASON, and a placement layer that dropped one of them would show half of it.

subject_places.name: The Negus, whose delegation arrives first, at line 88
subject_places.note: NO ID, AND THE REASON IS DIFFERENT FROM THE OTHER TWO: `ngs²yn` is a TITLE, the Negus of Aksum, and the text names no place at all for him. It is recorded here because this corpus now holds `africa-06-ezana-rie189`, an Aksumite king speaking in Ge‘ez, curated the same day — and because the stone lists the Negus BEFORE Rome.
